item.title: SharePoint CVE-2026-55040 Exploited as Adobe Commerce CVE-2026-71362 and Armored Likho Surface
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Aug 06:00 → 13 Aug 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-71362) Adobe Commerce Account Takeover via Session Identity Flaw — Must Read

CVE-2026-71362 is a critical Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source authorization flaw that can let unauthenticated attackers take over customer sessions on public storefronts. Adobe has released fixes, and organizations should urgently inventory and patch all production and non-production stores while monitoring for exploitation.

  • CVE-2026-71362 is a critical incorrect authorization vulnerability in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source that can allow an unauthenticated attacker to switch an active session to a different customer account.
  • Adobe Commerce versions 2.4.4 through 2.4.9 and Magento Open Source versions 2.4.6 through 2.4.9 at the -2026-jul build and earlier are affected.
  • Adobe published bulletin APSB26-92 on August 11, 2026, with fixed -2026-aug builds for supported Adobe Commerce, Magento Open Source, and Adobe Commerce B2B lines.
  • Adobe says it is not aware of exploitation in the wild, while Sansec reports that its Shield web application firewall is already blocking exploitation attempts against this CVE.
  • The article recommends inventorying all Adobe Commerce and Magento hosts, deploying WAF coverage, invalidating active customer sessions after patching, monitoring logs for account or session switching, and scanning exposed stores for backdoors.

Technologies: cms, waf

Products: adobe-commerce, magento-open-source, adobe-commerce-b2b, sansec-shield, cycognito-platform

Vendors: adobe, sansec, cycognito

Attackers Exploit SharePoint Authentication Bypass After Public PoC Release — Must Read

Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-55040, a critical Microsoft SharePoint authentication bypass, after Rapid7 released public PoC code. Organizations should urgently apply Microsoft’s July 2026 patches to prevent unauthenticated attackers from impersonating SharePoint users or administrators.

  • Threat actors have begun exploiting CVE-2026-55040, a critical Microsoft SharePoint authentication bypass vulnerability, after the release of public proof-of-concept code.
  • Microsoft patched CVE-2026-55040 in its July 2026 Patch Tuesday updates and said the flaw could allow impersonation, file disclosure, and data modification.
  • Rapid7 said the vulnerability is caused by several issues in the JWT token validation pipeline and can allow an unauthenticated attacker to forge a valid token and impersonate any SharePoint site user.
  • Rapid7’s Python-based proof-of-concept uses a forged JWT token to query a target’s domain controller, enumerate users by SID, and locate a site administrator.
  • KEVIntel recorded 12 exploitation attempts since July 19, 2026, with eight occurring on August 12 and 13 from IP addresses in Hong Kong, Japan, the Netherlands, Taiwan, and the U.S.

Technologies: cms

Products: microsoft-sharepoint

Vendors: microsoft, rapid7, kevintel

Armored Likho expands its cyber-espionage toolkit — Must Read

Kaspersky researchers uncovered a new Armored Likho cyber-espionage campaign targeting Russia that uses a fake donation app to deploy the Rust-based Still Toolkit. Its new modules steal Telegram session data and perform covert audio surveillance, showing the group is expanding into a more cohesive and capable spying toolset.

  • Kaspersky discovered a May 2026 cyber-espionage campaign by Armored Likho, also known as Eagle Werewolf, targeting private individuals and organizations in Russia, including major corporations, the public sector, IT, and education.
  • The campaign starts with a fake donation service app built in Rust with the Tauri framework, which displays a legitimate-looking catalog while quietly decrypting and launching the next-stage payload.
  • The newly identified Still Toolkit includes Still Sync, a Rust-based tool that steals Telegram session data and can use it to pull chat logs, media files, user details, and information about chats, groups, and channels through the Telegram API.
  • The Still Toolkit also includes Still Audio, a Rust-based audio surveillance implant that detects speech, records conversations, encodes recordings with libmp3lame, and sends them to a command-and-control server.
  • Kaspersky attributes the campaign to Armored Likho based on overlaps with earlier campaigns, including identical dropper architecture, matching sysmarker generation logic, shared encryption algorithm and key, and similar infrastructure patterns.

Technologies: operating-system, source-control, backup

Products: telegram-desktop, telegram-api, github, windows, tauri, tokio, flatbuffers, grpc, shadow-copy, robocopy, libmp3lame

Vendors: telegram, github, microsoft, tauri, tokio, google, grpc-project, lame-project

item.title: City-Forum targets Salesforce and ServiceNow portals; WindRelay Android NFC fraud emerges
item.content:encoded:
Window: 12 Aug 22:00 → 13 Aug 02:00 UTC (4 hours)

"City-Forum" data-theft attacks target Salesforce, ServiceNow portals — Must Read

A campaign dubbed City-Forum is stealing data from misconfigured Salesforce Experience Cloud and ServiceNow customer portals that expose records to unauthenticated guest users. The activity is ongoing and appears to come from a single long-running Contabo-hosted IP, with defenders urged to lock down guest access, public APIs, self-registration, and portal search sources.

  • Reco says an ongoing data theft campaign dubbed City-Forum is using custom tools to steal data exposed to anonymous users through Salesforce Experience Cloud and ServiceNow customer portals.
  • The attacks have been traced to the IP address 158.220.87.79, hosted by German VPS provider Contabo and associated with the city-forum.com domain since at least March 2025.
  • Reco says the campaign is not exploiting vulnerabilities in Salesforce or ServiceNow, but is abusing overly permissive guest-user sharing rules, permissions, or portal configurations.
  • On Salesforce, the attacker targets Aura endpoints and newer Lightning Web Runtime sites to enumerate and retrieve records exposed to guest accounts.
  • On ServiceNow, the attacker targets the POST /api/now/sp/search?sysparm_cancelable=true endpoint to search Service Portals that allow guest access to data.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: salesforce-experience-cloud, servicenow-service-portal, salesforce-aura, lightning-web-runtime, salesforce-ui-api, experience-builder

Vendors: salesforce, servicenow, reco

Android malware combo takes out loans and relays victims' credit cards — Should Read

Attackers are combining the SpyNote Android RAT with new WindRelay NFC malware to remotely control victims’ phones, take out loans, and relay live payment card data for fraudulent transactions. The attack relies heavily on phone-based social engineering, including convincing victims to sideload an app, grant permissions, tap their card to the phone, and enter their PIN.

  • A new Android NFC relay malware called WindRelay is being used with the SpyNote remote administration tool to steal card data and send it to attackers in real time.
  • In an incident investigated by Group-IB, a fraudster impersonated a bank employee, convinced the victim to sideload SpyNote disguised as a legitimate app, and obtained Accessibility Service permissions for remote access to the Android device.
  • After gaining remote access, the attacker installed WindRelay, used the victim’s banking app to take out a loan in the victim’s name, and instructed the victim to tap their payment card on the phone and enter their PIN.
  • Group-IB said the activity occurred during a 13-minute phone call, and the transactions were approved using the PIN provided by the victim.
  • Group-IB identified almost two dozen WindRelay samples submitted to VirusTotal between November 2025 and July 2026, with targeting appearing focused on Czechia, Slovakia, and Slovenia.

Technologies: mobile-os, remote-access

Products: android, google-play, windrelay, spynote

Vendors: google, group-ib

What Does Preemptive Defense Look Like Inside an AI SOC? — Optional

Silent Push argues that AI-driven SOC workflows are only useful if they enrich alerts with preemptive infrastructure intelligence, not just reactive IOC feeds. Its pitch is that feeding agents IOFA and Context Graph data can help defenders identify staged adversary infrastructure before attacks launch.

  • The article argues that AI-assisted SOC workflows can produce faster wrong answers if they rely on stale or reactive data.
  • Silent Push says its Indicators of Future Attack map adversary infrastructure across DNS, IP ranges, behavioral fingerprints, and web content to surface staging infrastructure before campaigns deploy.
  • The Silent Push MCP Server lets analysts or agents ask plain-language questions about indicators, domains, or infrastructure patterns inside tools such as Claude and Cursor without writing SPQL or using a separate console.
  • Silent Push says its platform integrates with Splunk, Palo Alto XSOAR, Swimlane, Tines, ThreatConnect, Torq, and Sumo Logic so preemptive context can feed existing SIEM and SOAR workflows.
  • Silent Push says it identified staging domains tied to Salt Typhoon in May 2025, two months before public reporting on the first intrusions emerged in July 2025.

Technologies: siem, soar

item.title: Adobe Commerce CVE-2026-71362 Exploitation and Fake Chrome VPN Extensions
item.content:encoded:
Window: 12 Aug 18:00 → 12 Aug 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers exploit critical Adobe Commerce flaw to hijack customer accounts — Must Read

Attackers are already trying to exploit a critical Adobe Commerce and Magento flaw, CVE-2026-71362, that can let them hijack customer accounts without authentication. Site administrators should urgently apply Adobe’s August 2026 isolated security patches after updating to the latest supported -p release.

  • Attempts to exploit CVE-2026-71362 in Adobe Commerce and Magento have been detected, potentially allowing attackers to hijack customer accounts.
  • Adobe described CVE-2026-71362 as an incorrect authorization vulnerability that could allow elevated access to sensitive resources without authentication.
  • Sansec said its Shield web application firewall is already blocking exploitation attempts, despite Adobe saying it was not aware of exploits in the wild for the fixed flaws.
  • Sansec’s analysis of Adobe’s patch found that the flaw lets attackers switch a customer session to another customer account, giving access to the victim’s account and private customer data.
  • Website administrators are advised to apply the August 2026 security update for supported Commerce, Commerce B2B, and Magento release lines as soon as possible.

Technologies: cms, waf

Products: adobe-commerce, magento, adobe-commerce-b2b, sansec-shield

Vendors: adobe, sansec

Hundreds of fake Chrome VPN extensions route traffic through a proxy — Should Read

Researchers found 737 fake Chrome VPN/proxy extensions impersonating major brands and routing users’ browser traffic through a single operator’s SOCKS5 proxies, potentially exposing destinations, source IPs, and plaintext HTTP data. Google has removed some, but Socket says more than 500 remain available, so users should check for the listed extension IDs and reset Chrome proxy settings if needed.

  • Socket researchers found more than 737 Chrome Web Store extensions that impersonated well-known VPN and proxy services while routing users’ traffic through SOCKS5 proxies operated by a single provider.
  • The extensions impersonated brands including Proton VPN, NordVPN, Surfshark, ExpressVPN, and Cloudflare’s 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver.
  • The extensions were downloaded nearly 75,000 times, mainly by Russian users looking for tools to bypass blocked services in the country.
  • Socket identified behaviors including routing all browser traffic through SOCKS5 proxies on port 1082, resolving proxy hostnames through Cloudflare or Google DNS-over-HTTPS, and advertising nonexistent premium server locations for subscription fraud.
  • Google removed more than 200 related extensions, but Socket said over 500 were still available in the Chrome Web Store and recommended users remove any listed extensions and confirm Chrome’s proxy configuration is normal.

Technologies: browser, vpn, proxy

Products: google-chrome, chrome-web-store, proton-vpn, nordvpn, surfshark, expressvpn, cloudflare-1.1.1.1, google-public-dns

Vendors: google, cloudflare, proton, nordvpn, surfshark, expressvpn

The Human Risk Layer of AI — Optional

AI agents now act like workforce members with access, data, and decision-making authority, so securing them requires managing human risk as well as technical controls. The paper argues that Human Risk Management helps close the gap between what AI systems can do and how employees will actually use them.

  • The article presents a white paper titled “The Human Risk Layer of AI,” dated August 12, 2026.
  • The paper focuses on why securing large language models requires more than technical controls.
  • The article states that AI agents can access data, use internal systems, generate code, send communications, summarize documents, and execute multi-step workflows for human operators.
  • The article says AI agents are indistinguishable from a workforce member with credentials for security purposes.
  • The paper is presented by Living Security, which is identified as a Health-ISAC Community Services Champion.

Vendors: living-security

item.title: Lazarus Exploits CVE-2026-68820 as Windows Plug and Play Attacks Surface
item.content:encoded:
Window: 12 Aug 14:00 → 12 Aug 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Lazarus hackers exploited Windows zero-day to target defense firms — Must Read

North Korean Lazarus hackers exploited a Windows zero-day, CVE-2026-68820, to gain SYSTEM privileges and deploy updated FudModule rootkits against defense, aerospace, and aviation targets in Operation Dream Job. The campaign also used new Troy backdoor malware and compromised Roundcube servers to hide malicious communications.

  • North Korean Lazarus hackers exploited Windows zero-day CVE-2026-68820 in Operation Dream Job attacks targeting defense-sector companies.
  • Microsoft patched CVE-2026-68820 in its August 2026 Patch Tuesday updates and said the flaw is an actively exploited use-after-free issue in Windows AFD.sys that can allow local privilege escalation to SYSTEM.
  • Check Point found that Lazarus used an exploit for CVE-2026-68820 in a new version of the FudModule kernel-mode rootkit, specifically supporting Windows 11 builds 26100 and 26200.
  • The latest Operation Dream Job activity targeted defense, aerospace, and aviation organizations in Europe and India through fraudulent recruitment offers, with successful targeting observed in France and Germany and activity extending to Brazil.
  • Check Point also reported a new Lazarus backdoor called Troy and compromised Roundcube installations infected with a PHP web shell called RelayShell.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows, windows-11, afd.sys, smart-app-control, roundcube

Vendors: microsoft, check-point, roundcube

Plug and Pwn attack uses fake USB devices for Windows SYSTEM access — Should Read

Researchers showed that Windows Plug and Play can be abused with fake USB devices, or even RDP USB redirection, to make Windows install vulnerable vendor software and gain SYSTEM privileges. Disabling co-installers helps against some chains, but sensitive environments should also restrict device installation and disable unnecessary PnP redirection.

  • Security researchers Alejandro Hernando and Borja Martínez disclosed “Plug and Pwn” attacks that abuse Windows Plug and Play to make Windows install vulnerable or insecure vendor software and gain NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges.
  • The researchers used FaceDancer with Cynthion and GreatFET hardware to emulate USB devices, causing Windows to recognize the fake hardware and install associated vendor driver packages.
  • One demonstrated zero-click physical attack impersonated Sierra Wireless and Sony FeliCa devices against a fully updated Windows 11 computer with nobody logged in, taking approximately five minutes to obtain a SYSTEM reverse shell.
  • The researchers also demonstrated “NoPlug & Pwn,” which abuses RDP USB redirection with a Python RDP client to make a remote Windows host enumerate a fake USB device and install driver software as SYSTEM.
  • Setting the DisableCoInstallers registry value can disrupt some demonstrated attacks, but Hernando said it does not stop the broader attack class because Plug and Play enumeration, Windows Update resolution, driver staging, INF processing, and INF-installed services remain exposed.

Technologies: operating-system, remote-access

Products: windows, windows-plug-and-play, windows-update, remote-desktop-protocol, facedancer, cynthion, greatfet, razer-synapse, sony-felica, intel-realsense

Vendors: microsoft, razer, sierra-wireless, sony, intel, wacom, atheros, great-scott-gadgets

737 Chrome VPN Extensions Caught Routing Traffic Through Proxies. Check If You Have One — Should Read

Researchers found 737 Chrome VPN/proxy extensions, many impersonating major VPN brands, that routed users’ browser traffic through SOCKS5 proxies controlled by a single operator, exposing browsing destinations and some unencrypted data. Users should check for and remove suspicious or brand-impersonating Chrome VPN extensions.

  • Researchers found 737 free VPN and proxy Chrome extensions that mainly targeted Russian-speaking users seeking access to blocked services and routed browser traffic through proxy infrastructure.
  • The extensions were published across at least 40 Chrome Web Store developer accounts and accumulated 75,486 installs.
  • Socket reported that 274 of the extensions impersonated 66 established VPN and privacy brands, including Proton VPN, NordVPN, Surfshark, AdGuard VPN, Browsec, ExpressVPN, CyberGhost, Windscribe, TunnelBear, Cloudflare’s 1.1.1.1, and Google’s Outline.
  • Most of the extensions set Chrome’s proxy settings to a fixed SOCKS5 server on port 1082, allowing the operator to observe browser destinations, source IP addresses, TLS SNI values, and any request body sent over plain HTTP.
  • Netskope Threat Labs also reported that the Chrome extension “AI Sidebar with Deepseek, ChatGPT, Claude, and more.” returned with a monetization payload that opens an affiliate link every time the extension updates or uninstalls.

Technologies: browser, vpn, proxy

Products: google-chrome, chrome-web-store, proton-vpn, nordvpn, surfshark, adguard-vpn, browsec, expressvpn, cyberghost, windscribe, tunnelbear, cloudflare-1.1.1.1, outline, ai-sidebar-with-deepseek-chatgpt-claude-and-more

Vendors: google, socket, netskope, proton, nordvpn, surfshark, adguard, browsec, expressvpn, cyberghost, windscribe, tunnelbear, cloudflare

Blacklight: Illuminating AI Agent Artifacts for Attackers and Defenders — May Read

SpecterOps released Blacklight, an open-source toolkit for discovering and analyzing local AI agent artifacts from tools like Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and Antigravity CLI. The key takeaway is that these endpoint artifacts can expose credentials, sessions, project context, and trust relationships, so defenders should inventory and monitor them like other high-value local application data.

  • Blacklight is an open-source security research toolkit from SpecterOps for discovering and analyzing AI agent artifacts that reside on endpoints.
  • Blacklight currently maps artifacts across Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and Antigravity CLI.
  • Local AI agent artifacts can expose authentication material, configuration settings, session and chat content, session indexes, workspace metadata, rules and permissions, local databases, and external integrations.
  • Blacklight Scout provides endpoint triage to identify supported agent roots, valuable artifacts to collect first, and ranked session-file candidates without reading artifact bodies in its quiet loaders.
  • The defender guidance includes osquery inventory and monitoring content, Windows Security Event 4663 guidance for read detection, and references to provider compliance APIs such as the OpenAI Compliance Platform and Claude Compliance Activity Feed.

Technologies: database, operating-system, siem

Products: blacklight, codex, claude-code, cursor, antigravity-cli, gemini, osquery, nemesis, trufflehog, euphony, mythic, apollo, poseidon, openai-compliance-platform, claude-compliance-activity-feed

Vendors: specterops, openai, anthropic, cursor, google, osquery, trufflesecurity

FBI: Hackers target online accounts to steal nude photos — Optional

The FBI warns that criminals are hacking social media and online accounts to steal explicit photos and videos, then using them for sextortion, harassment, or sale on criminal marketplaces. It urges users, including student-athletes, to avoid sharing verification codes or password-reset links, use strong passwords, enable MFA, and avoid storing explicit content in internet-accessible accounts.

  • The FBI warned that cybercriminals are targeting adults’ and children’s social media and other online accounts to steal sexually explicit images or videos.
  • The FBI said stolen explicit content may be used to blackmail victims, sold on criminal marketplaces, or paired with personal information to enable further harassment, sextortion, stalking, or targeted attacks.
  • The FBI and the National Collegiate Athletic Association warned that student-athletes’ online accounts are also being targeted in similar sexual exploitation schemes.
  • The FBI advised potential victims not to respond to messages asking for verification codes or password reset links, and warned that legitimate platforms will not request verification codes, temporary passwords, or PIN reset codes.
  • The FBI recommended using complex passwords, enabling multi-factor authentication when possible, and avoiding storage of explicit photos or videos on social media accounts or Internet-accessible sites.

Technologies: mfa

Cybersecurity in the Lab — Optional

Health-ISAC’s Phil Englert warns that laboratory environments face distinct cybersecurity risks, especially around connected medical devices and lab systems, and should not be overlooked in enterprise security planning. The article highlights key risks and practical recommendations for improving lab cyber resilience.

  • The article focuses on cybersecurity risks that are unique to laboratory environments compared to other healthcare settings.
  • Phil Englert, Health-ISAC Vice President of Medical Device Security, discusses three major risks that laboratories should be aware of.
  • The article also mentions that Phil Englert provides recommendations related to laboratory cybersecurity.
  • The Health-ISAC post directs readers to read the full article in Medical Laboratory Observer.

The Threat Hiding in Your Hiring Process: How Fake Remote Workers Get In — Optional

Fake remote workers, including North Korean IT operatives, can bypass hiring checks by using false identities, proxies, and remote-access setups to gain legitimate corporate access. Organizations should treat identity proofing as an access control by verifying the live person receiving credentials during onboarding and service-desk workflows.

  • The US Department of State warned in July that North Korean IT workers impersonate nationals of other countries to obtain work and send salaries back to parent agencies in North Korea.
  • The FBI has warned that fraudulent workers may use legitimate employment access to copy source-code repositories, exfiltrate proprietary information, support other cybercriminal activity, and attempt extortion after discovery or dismissal.
  • Fake remote-worker operations can satisfy separate hiring controls by using stolen or proxy-supplied documents, fabricated résumés, proxy interviewees, facilitator addresses, laptop farms, and third-party payroll accounts.
  • Warning signs of a fake remote worker include frequent changes to registered information, payment account name mismatches, multiple accounts using the same ID, unusual IP address patterns, and unusually high hours logged.
  • Specops says its Secure Onboarding product combines government-issued identity-document scanning with biometric liveness detection to help confirm that the person completing onboarding matches the identity document.

Technologies: iam, identity-provider

Products: specops-secure-onboarding, specops-password-policy, active-directory

Vendors: specops-software, microsoft

We're unbundling Castle, and IP intelligence is the first piece — Optional

Castle has launched its standalone IP Intelligence API, letting teams access its underlying data on IP connection types, ASN/location, and observed proxy or VPN tunnels without buying the full Castle platform. The service supports live lookups, batch queries, and downloadable proxy feeds for fraud and abuse detection workflows.

  • Castle is separating its platform from the underlying intelligence data, starting with a standalone IP intelligence API that is live now.
  • The IP intelligence API is free to sign up for and costs $0.001 per lookup after the free quota.
  • Castle says the API can identify whether an IP address is an ordinary home connection, a datacenter, a mobile carrier, or a rented residential proxy.
  • The API response keeps address, ASN, location, and tunnel observations separate, including proxy or VPN operator details and the time the observation was last confirmed.
  • The service supports live lookups, batch queries of up to 1,000 addresses, and downloadable precomputed tunnel feeds for 1-day, 7-day, 30-day, or 60-day windows.

Products: castle-ip-intelligence-api

Vendors: castle

item.title: Microsoft CVE-2026-68820 Lazarus Exploitation, SharePoint CVE-2026-55040 Attacks, and Defender ShieldBreak
item.content:encoded:
Window: 12 Aug 10:00 → 12 Aug 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers leverage new Microsoft SharePoint exploit in attacks — Must Read

Attackers are already using Rapid7’s public proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-55040, a critical Microsoft SharePoint JWT authentication bypass that can let unauthenticated attackers impersonate users or admins. Organizations running affected SharePoint servers should apply Microsoft’s July 2026 patches and avoid exposing SharePoint directly to the Internet.

  • A proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-55040, a critical Microsoft SharePoint authentication bypass vulnerability, was published by Rapid7 on Tuesday and is already being used in attacks.
  • CVE-2026-55040 affects SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016 and SharePoint Server 2019 and can let unauthenticated attackers perform operations as a SharePoint site user or administrator.
  • Microsoft patched CVE-2026-55040 in the July 2026 Patch Tuesday updates and said exploitation could allow an attacker to disclose files and modify data without impacting system availability.
  • Defused reported that attackers are using Rapid7’s proof-of-concept code against its SharePoint honeypots.
  • CISA urged security teams to avoid directly exposing SharePoint servers to the Internet unless necessary and to follow Microsoft’s SharePoint Server security-hardening guidance.

Technologies: cms

Products: microsoft-sharepoint, sharepoint-enterprise-server-2016, sharepoint-server-2019

Vendors: microsoft, rapid7

CISA gives federal agencies two weeks to patch Microsoft bug exploited in DPRK campaign — Must Read

CISA ordered federal agencies to patch a Microsoft Windows Winsock vulnerability by August 25 after it was exploited by North Korea’s Lazarus Group in Operation Dream Job attacks targeting defense and aerospace job seekers. The bug lets attackers who already gained a foothold through phishing escalate privileges to take full control of affected Windows systems.

  • CISA gave federal agencies until August 25 to patch CVE-2026-68820, a Windows Winsock vulnerability that Microsoft confirmed is being exploited in real-world attacks.
  • The vulnerability requires a device restart to fix, has no workaround, and was the only bug in Microsoft’s Patch Tuesday release confirmed as actively exploited.
  • Check Point said Lazarus Group hackers used fake recruiter approaches tied to Operation Dream Job, impersonating organizations such as Lockheed Martin and Enveil before sending malicious PDF files to targets.
  • According to Check Point, the malicious files enable a backdoor that gives Lazarus Group long-term remote access and then deploy an exploit for CVE-2026-68820 to escalate control on the infected machine.
  • Researchers found targets across several defense sectors, including surveillance sensors, drones and robotics, in France, Germany, Brazil and India.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows, winsock

Vendors: microsoft, check-point

Adobe Patches Three CVSS 10.0 ColdFusion and Campaign Classic Flaws — Must Read

Adobe released urgent patches for critical flaws in ColdFusion, Commerce, and Campaign Classic, including three CVSS 10.0 issues that could allow arbitrary code execution. Admins should apply the ColdFusion and Campaign Classic updates within 72 hours, though Adobe says there is no evidence of active exploitation.

  • Adobe shipped updates for critical vulnerabilities affecting ColdFusion, Commerce, and Campaign Classic that could lead to arbitrary code execution and privilege escalation.
  • The most severe issues include CVE-2026-48362 in ColdFusion and CVE-2026-71398 and CVE-2026-27302 in Campaign Classic, each with a CVSS score of 10.0.
  • ColdFusion fixes are included in versions 2025.0.12 and 2023.0.23, while Campaign Classic fixes are included in ACC v7 7.4.4 build 9400.
  • The ColdFusion and Campaign Classic updates have a Priority 1 rating, indicating vulnerabilities with a higher risk of being targeted by malicious cyber attacks.
  • Adobe said there is no evidence that the flaws have been exploited in the wild, but administrators are advised to install the updates as soon as possible, preferably within 72 hours.

Technologies: cms

Products: adobe-coldfusion, adobe-commerce, adobe-campaign-classic

Vendors: adobe

New Microsoft Defender 'ShieldBreak' zero-day grants SYSTEM privileges — Should Read

A researcher released a Microsoft Defender zero-day exploit called ShieldBreak that can grant SYSTEM privileges on fully patched Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server systems. The exploit appears to bypass Microsoft’s earlier RoguePlanet patch, and Microsoft has not yet issued a fix.

  • A security researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse released a new Microsoft Defender zero-day exploit named ShieldBreak after Microsoft released the August 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates.
  • Nightmare Eclipse said ShieldBreak can gain SYSTEM privileges on fully patched Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server systems.
  • Cybersecurity expert Kevin Beaumont said ShieldBreak works differently from RoguePlanet, using a user-mode callback hook to change file contents during a Defender cloud-hydration scan via the Cloud Filter API.
  • Will Dormann confirmed that the ShieldBreak exploit works and said Microsoft Defender needs to be enabled for the exploit to escalate attackers’ privileges.
  • The ShieldBreak release is part of an ongoing dispute between Microsoft and Nightmare Eclipse over Microsoft’s vulnerability disclosure and bug bounty practices.

Technologies: antivirus, operating-system

Products: microsoft-defender, windows-10, windows-11, windows-server, windows-server-2025, cloud-filter-api

Vendors: microsoft

OpenAI, Anthropic, Google API Flaw Let Weaker AI Models Decode Stronger Models' Reasoning — Should Read

Researchers found that encrypted AI reasoning blocks from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google APIs could be replayed across sessions and decoded by weaker compatible models, exposing hidden reasoning and secrets from published agent logs. The attacks have reportedly been mitigated, but developers should strip opaque reasoning data before sharing API transcripts.

  • Researchers disclosed a flaw in how OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google carried hidden AI reasoning between API calls, allowing internal reasoning and secrets from session logs to be recovered.
  • The weakness involved encrypted reasoning objects that could be replayed into another session and, in testing, given to a weaker model in the same provider family to reveal hidden content.
  • Across 6,708 public agent trajectories, the team decoded 315,320 thinking blocks and found 704 distinct privacy artifacts from genuine user sessions after excluding benchmark sources.
  • The recovered artifacts included 62 API keys, 33 passwords, 24 access tokens, seven private keys, and 64 items that appeared only in hidden reasoning and not in visible traces.
  • The researchers reported the issue to affected providers and said the demonstrated attacks stopped working after mitigations, but no public vendor acknowledgment has surfaced in the article.

Products: openai-api, anthropic-api, gemini-api, claude-haiku-4-5, gpt-5-6-luna, gemini-robotics-er-1-6

Vendors: openai, anthropic, google, microsoft, hugging-face

WS-Trust Autologon Endpoint: Password Spray Without Smart Lockout Blocking — Should Read

A legacy Microsoft Entra ID WS-Trust autologon endpoint can be abused to password spray accounts without triggering Smart Lockout or standard sign-in logs, while still revealing when a password is valid even if MFA or Conditional Access blocks login. Defenders should disable WS-Trust/usernamemixed or block legacy authentication and monitor Unified Audit Logs for autologon activity.

  • The article describes how Microsoft Entra ID’s legacy WS-Trust autologon endpoint for Seamless SSO can accept direct username and password requests from the internet.
  • Testing found that password spray attempts through the autologon endpoint bypassed Smart Lockout, with more than 1,000 failed attempts against one account from a single unfamiliar IP without receiving a locked-account response.
  • Failed authentication attempts against the autologon endpoint did not appear in standard Entra ID sign-in logs, though the article says the Unified Audit Log can capture requests to autologon.microsoftazuread-sso.com.
  • The endpoint returns different AADSTS error codes that can distinguish wrong passwords from valid passwords blocked later by MFA, Conditional Access, or password-expiration requirements.
  • The article recommends disabling the usernamemixed endpoint, blocking legacy authentication through Conditional Access, enabling Unified Audit Log alerts for autologon requests, and moving accounts toward passwordless sign-in methods.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, mfa, cloud-platform

The key lesson is that messages with no visible links and benign file verdicts can still hide phishing logic that runs client-side after user interaction.

  • Opening the attachment displayed a fake Microsoft SharePoint secure access page with a locked document label and a form asking the recipient to enter a work address.
  • The attachment’s inline script built the destination URL only after form submission, using Google redirect endpoints and a base64-encoded recipient address in the fragment.

Tracking Shai-Hulud: Inside the ChainDrop NPM Worm — Must Read

ChainDrop is a fast-spreading npm worm that compromised trusted GitHub release pipelines to publish malicious packages with valid provenance attestations, then stole developer tokens to infect hundreds more packages. The key takeaway is that signed/SLSA-proven builds do not prove software is safe when attackers control the source repo or CI pipeline.

  • ChainDrop entered the npm ecosystem on August 4, 2026 through a compromised maintainer account for the keyv ecosystem.
  • The attacker modified legitimate GitHub repositories and release workflows so poisoned packages, including keyv, cacheable, flat-cache, and file-entry-cache, were published to npm with valid provenance attestations.
  • Aikido Security researchers found that ChainDrop propagated to more than 400 packages by stealing npm tokens and republishing infected versions of packages those tokens could access.
  • ChainDrop used an Ethereum smart contract to retrieve active command-and-control domains, allowing the attacker to rotate domains without changing the deployed malware.
  • The worm planted persistence hooks in Claude Code and VS Code configuration files, allowing the payload to re-execute when a developer opened a project or started an AI-agent session.

  • The attackers compromised vulnerable Roundcube webmail servers using CVE-2025-49113 and deployed RelayShell, a PHP webshell that turned compromised web servers into command-and-control relay nodes.
